q: When you send an image to a vision-capable chat model, what do you usually include in the same message?
opts: A question or instruction about it
A neural voice for the spoken description
A key for the storage account of the image
exp: A user message typically combines the image with a text part that says what you want, such as 'List the damaged parts'. Voices are for text to speech, storage keys must never be sent to a model, and the deployment type is a setting of the deployment, not part of a message.

ctx: Customers of an insurance company upload photos of damaged cars. The claims system needs JSON with a list of damaged parts and a severity for each one.
q: Which approach fits best?
opts: Convert the photos to speech with text to speech and transcribe it
Run key phrase extraction on the file names of all the photos
Send each photo with a JSON schema to a vision-capable model
Use a Global Batch deployment of an embedding model for photos
exp: A vision-capable model can interpret the damage, and structured outputs with a JSON schema make it return exactly the fields the claims system expects. Text to speech and key phrase extraction do not look at images, and an embedding model returns vectors, not damage reports.

q: For each of the following statements about visual input, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: A vision-capable model can explain a screenshot of an error message.
A message can contain one image at most.
Sending an image means that the model's response will also be an image.
exp: Yes for the first: the model can read the error text in a screenshot and explain it. No for the second: a message can contain several image parts. No for the third: vision-capable chat models return text; creating images needs an image-generation model.

q: Complete the sentences about visual input.
tpl: A model that accepts both text and images is called {0}. An image can be sent as a URL or as {1} data.
exp: Multimodal models work with more than one type of input, such as text and images. Images can be referenced by URL or embedded in the request as base64-encoded data in a data URL. Monolingual and serverless describe other things, and zip files or encryption alone are not accepted image formats.

q: Which prompt is most likely to produce the image you want?
opts: An image, please, as good as you can possibly make it
Make it nice and beautiful so that everyone will love it
A cozy reading corner by a window, watercolor style
exp: Good image prompts describe the subject, setting and style, which gives the model clear guidance. Vague prompts, whether they are long or short, leave almost everything to chance, so results are unpredictable and rarely match what you had in mind.

q: A designer needs a logo draft from gpt-image-1 with a transparent background. Which request parameter should be set?
opts: temperature set to 0 for the logo
exp: gpt-image-1 supports a background parameter; setting it to transparent, with an output format that supports transparency such as PNG, produces an image without a solid background. temperature, top_p and stop are text-generation settings and do not affect image backgrounds.

q: Match each requirement to the right approach. Each approach can be used once or not at all.
items: Create a new poster from a description
Change only the sky in an existing photo
Describe what an existing photo shows
Read the words on a sign in a photo
targets: Image generation from a text prompt
Image captioning or a multimodal chat model
exp: A new poster comes from image generation, changing only part of a photo uses editing with a mask, describing a photo uses captioning or a multimodal model, and reading words on a sign uses OCR. Speech synthesis creates audio and fits none of these requirements.

q: Which THREE are responsible practices when you publish AI-generated images? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Remove all provenance information from the files
Keep the Content Credentials so viewers can see that the image is AI-generated
Claim that the images are real photographs
Review the images for errors and harmful content before publishing
Check that the images do not copy protected characters or brands
exp: Content Credentials show that an image is AI-generated, a review catches errors and harmful content, and a check for protected characters or brands avoids legal problems. Removing provenance information and claiming that images are real photographs mislead viewers.

q: Which VisualFeatures value should you request to get the text in an image with ImageAnalysisClient?
exp: VisualFeatures.READ runs OCR and returns the text as blocks, lines and words with their positions. TAGS returns keywords, PEOPLE returns bounding boxes for people, and SMART_CROPS suggests crop regions.

q: Image Analysis returns many tags for each photo, and some are wrong. The app should display only reliable tags. What should it do?
opts: Show only tags whose confidence is above a threshold
Show every tag and let users decide which are right
exp: Each tag comes with a confidence score, so the app can keep only tags above a threshold chosen through testing. Showing everything includes the unreliable tags, and Image Analysis has no temperature setting; quota controls throughput, not accuracy.

q: For each of the following statements about ImageAnalysisClient, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: It can return a newly generated image.
Each call returns one visual feature, so a caption and tags need separate calls.
It can analyze image bytes, while an image at a URL must be downloaded first.
exp: No for the first: Image Analysis describes images and does not create new ones. No for the second: visual_features accepts a list, such as CAPTION, TAGS and READ together. No for the third: analyze() takes image bytes and analyze_from_url() takes a URL.

q: Complete the Python code that analyzes a local image with key authentication.
tpl:
client = ImageAnalysisClient(
    endpoint=endpoint,
    credential={0}(key),
)
result = client.{1}(image_data=image_bytes, visual_features=[VisualFeatures.TAGS])
exp: AzureKeyCredential wraps the resource key, and analyze() takes the image bytes through image_data. DefaultAzureCredential uses Microsoft Entra ID and does not take a key, SpeechConfig is for the Speech SDK, analyze_from_url() needs a URL, and generate is not an Image Analysis method.

q: Which THREE requirements point to Image Analysis rather than a multimodal chat model? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: A friendly explanation of why a meme is funny
OCR lines with their exact positions on the page
A back-and-forth conversation about a photo
Bounding boxes for each detected person
exp: Exact OCR positions, person bounding boxes and smart crops are structured results that Image Analysis returns. Explaining a joke and holding a conversation about a photo need open-ended language, which suits a multimodal chat model.

q: What does Content Understanding's content extraction produce from a document?
opts: An MP3 file with the text read aloud
A new image of each page in color
exp: Content extraction turns the document into Markdown that preserves structure such as paragraphs, headings and tables, which is useful for search and as input for field extraction. It does not produce audio, images or deployments.

q: An invoice analyzer's vendor_name field sometimes returns the customer's name instead of the supplier's. What should you change first?
opts: Change the field type from string to boolean
Improve the description of the field
Increase the quota of the model deployment
exp: Field descriptions guide the models that fill each field, so a precise description that distinguishes the issuer from the customer usually fixes the confusion; labeled examples can help further. A boolean type cannot hold a name, deleting the field loses the data, and quota does not affect accuracy.

q: Match each invoice field to the field type that fits it. Each type can be used once or not at all.
exp: A total is a number, an invoice date is a date, a paid or unpaid flag is a boolean, and repeating line items with several values each are an array of objects. Image is not a field type for extracted invoice values.

q: For each of the following statements about Content Understanding, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Documents must be typed; scanned images are not supported.
A field schema lets you name the values you want back.
exp: No for the first: OCR reads scanned pages and images, including handwriting. Yes for the second: the schema defines the field names, types and descriptions that the analyzer returns. Yes for the third: PDFs are a supported document input.

q: A RAG solution misses facts that appear only in charts inside PDF reports. Which Content Understanding capability helps?
opts: Speech synthesis of the report text
Figure analysis of charts and diagrams
exp: Figure analysis describes the content of charts and diagrams in text, so the information becomes searchable and can be retrieved for RAG. Speech synthesis produces audio, smart crops suggests thumbnails, and key phrase extraction works on text that is already extracted.

q: Which file can you send to a Content Understanding image analyzer?
exp: Image analyzers take image files such as JPEG or PNG. WAV recordings go to audio analyzers, MP4 videos to video analyzers, and spreadsheets are not image inputs.

q: Complete the sentences about fields in an analyzer for shelf photos.
tpl: For a field whose value must be Full, Partly empty or Empty, use the {0} method. For a free-text description of problems on the shelf, use the {1} method.
exp: Classify picks one value from a list you define, which suits Full, Partly empty or Empty. Generate creates free-form values, such as a description. Extract returns values printed in documents and is not supported for images.

q: Which TWO changes are most likely to improve the results of a Content Understanding image analyzer? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Set a higher temperature in the analyzer
Write clear descriptions for each field
Remove all fields from the schema
Define the list of categories for each classify field
Send MP3 files instead of images
exp: Clear field descriptions tell the models exactly what to produce, and explicit category lists keep classification consistent. Analyzers are configured through schemas rather than a temperature setting, a schema without fields returns no fields, and MP3 files are audio, not images.

q: Which business scenario is a good fit for Content Understanding audio analysis?
opts: Designing a new logo for the call center
Building a macro for a sales spreadsheet
Post-call analytics for a call center
Resizing the photos of the agents' badges
exp: Audio analysis transcribes recordings and produces fields such as summaries, sentiment and topics, which is exactly what post-call analytics needs. Logo design, spreadsheet macros and photo resizing do not involve analyzing audio.

q: A media company wants to find every segment of its videos where one of its products appears, and tag those segments. What should it use?
opts: Key phrase extraction on the names of the video files
A video analyzer with a per-segment field for the products
exp: A video analyzer splits the video into segments and fills fields for each one, so a field such as products_shown tags where each product appears. File names do not show what is in the video, and speech synthesis and image generation create content instead of analyzing it.

q: For each of the following statements about audio and video analysis, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Audio analysis distinguishes different speakers in a recording.
A video is converted to a PDF before it can be analyzed.
Video analysis uses both what is shown and what is said.
exp: Yes for the first: transcripts can label different speakers, which is useful for calls and meetings. No for the second: video files are analyzed directly. Yes for the third: video analysis combines keyframes and visual content with the transcript of the audio track.

q: Match each requirement for analyzing lecture and meeting videos to the capability that meets it. Each capability can be used once or not at all.
items: Know when each scene starts and ends
Read the text on slides shown in a lecture video
Know what each person said in a meeting
Get a one-line summary of each scene
targets: A generated field for each segment
exp: Scene boundaries come from segmentation, slide text from OCR on keyframes, who said what from a transcript with speaker labels, and per-scene summaries from a generated field for each segment. Image generation creates new pictures and does not analyze videos.

q: How can an app use the grounding information that Content Understanding returns for each field?
opts: Delete the source file after the analysis is done
Change the model deployment when a value is wrong
Show reviewers where each value came from
exp: Grounding identifies the region of the source content behind each value, so a review screen can highlight it and a person can confirm or correct the value quickly. It is not used to delete files, change deployments or adjust quota.

q: Which tool is designed to help you improve custom Content Understanding analyzers by labeling data?
opts: Power BI with an AI visual
exp: Content Understanding Studio complements the Foundry portal with an experience for improving analyzer performance, including labeling data and building classification-based analyzers. Azure Advisor gives recommendations, Power BI builds reports, and Azure Policy enforces resource rules.

q: Complete the sentence about calling Content Understanding from a production app.
tpl: The app should authenticate with {0}, start the analyze operation for each file, and then {1} until the result is ready.
exp: Production apps should use Microsoft Entra ID, for example through a managed identity, instead of unauthenticated or public access. Because analysis is a long-running operation, the app polls the returned operation URL until the status shows the result is ready. Restarting the analyzer or rereading the request does not give you the result.

q: You are building a pipeline that makes PDF reports searchable for a RAG chat app. Put the steps in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Store the chunks and their vectors in a search index
Generate a new image for each document
Analyze each document with Content Understanding to get Markdown and figure descriptions
Split the Markdown into chunks and create embeddings
exp: Documents are uploaded first, then Content Understanding turns them into Markdown with figure descriptions, the text is split into chunks and embedded, and finally the chunks and vectors are indexed for retrieval. Generating new images adds nothing to a search pipeline.
